images.caption: Fig. 1:The failure loop. RL trains a policy warm-started from Contact-GraspNet in 256 parallel environments. Grasps it keeps failing (orange) go to VR, where a person shows two grasp points; points verified with the robot’s hand retrain the policy from the same warm start. Bottom: the final policy on unseen objects.
Fig. 2:A simulated grasp by the floating Franka hand (settle, insert, close, lift). RL + demos acts on a held-out power drill;c1c_{1}andc2c_{2}are its predicted contacts.

Fig. 3:Human grasp points (orange) and a failed RL grasp (blue) on one demonstrated case per family, chosen where RL + demos improved most, so not a representative sample. Gray: object surface points.

Fig. 9:One sorting step by the Franka arm with the RL + demos policy. (a) The policy receives 128 points of the cup’s segment (blue; gray: the rest of the observed segment) and outputs two contacts (orange, cyan) and an approach (green). (b)–(e) The arm inserts along the approach, closes, lifts, and places the cup in the household bin, on the first try. The cup is a test object not seen in training.
